title: ConnectorSurface runs a connector call without checking it against the tool's schema
body:
## Summary
Tier 3 calls in the journey are never validated against the connector tool's inputSchema, while every tier 1 call is validated at dispatch (inject.js checkInput) and the production catalog validates both.

## Description
examples/journey/src/connector-surface.ts:102 hands params straight to port.call; examples/journey/src/connectors/port.ts:37 and :48 publish open schemas ({ type: "object", properties } with no additionalProperties: false and no required). A page tool's call goes through packages/athena-bridge/inject.js:114 checkInput and the kit door, and in the product src/athena/core/catalog.py validates call input for every tier. So a beat that misspells a connector argument (search_mail { q } instead of { query }) passes in the journey with an empty search, and only fails against a real connector. mcp-tools/tool-schema-design: the published schema is the enforced one. Fixed: close the fakes' schemas (required + additionalProperties: false) and have ConnectorSurface.run refuse with validator_failed, writing its row, before port.call - reusing the kit's validateArgs (examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/door.ts) the way contracts.ts already imports the demo-kit seed by relative path.

## Flow
- journey/take beat calls mailer.read("search_mail", { q: "availability" })
- ConnectorSurface.run -> FakeMail.call: params.query undefined -> "" -> every message matches
- the beat asserts on a search that never ran as written; the real connector would refuse
- fix: validate in ConnectorSurface.run against port.listTools() schemas, closed, before the egress check

## Expected impact
Whoever edits a connector beat learns about a wrong argument in the journey rather than on stage. Could break: any of the 19 connector calls in journey.spec.ts/take.spec.ts whose arguments do not match the fakes' schemas - the probe must list them first.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a tier 3 call is held to its schema exactly as a tier 1 call is
Before: 0 of 19 connector calls in journey.spec.ts/take.spec.ts pass through any validator (the args probe in this round skipped them: 'not a page tool: append_to_page, create_page, search_mail, send_mail')
After: not built - needs the schemas closed and a validator wired in two files plus the 19 calls checked
Method: simulation - three walked cases (a misspelled query, an extra key, a missing to) all reach port.call today; the probe that would decide it (the round's probe-args extended to port.listTools()) was not built
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extend the round's probe-args.mjs to validate the 19 connector calls against port.listTools() closed schemas, plus a seeded misspelled-argument control that must refuse

title: narrate --dry overwrites the measured lengths of clips already on disk
body:
## Summary
A dry run writes word-count estimates into take/audio/durations.json for every beat in scope, replacing the ffprobe-measured length of an mp3 that is still on disk.

## Description
examples/journey/scripts/narrate.mjs:376 sets durations[beat.id] = <estimate> for every beat in scope and writes the merged file; the measured lengths written at :484 for clips that exist are overwritten. src/script.ts loadDurations treats every positive entry as measured, and scripts/compose.mjs lays the real mp3 at the beat. So `pnpm narrate -- --dry` after a real narration (README: 'no network: estimated durations only, so the recorder can run') makes the next take hold each beat for the estimate while compose plays the real clip over it. Fixed: a dry run leaves an entry alone when its mp3 is on disk (or writes estimates only for beats with no clip).

## Flow
- pnpm narrate (real): durations.json B = 6120 ms (ffprobe), take/audio/B.mp3 on disk
- pnpm narrate -- --dry: durations.json B = 4000 ms (word estimate)
- the take holds B for 4000 + breath; compose lays the 6120 ms clip from B's start
- the clip runs 2 s into the next beat's picture

## Expected impact
Whoever re-takes after a dry rehearsal gets audio over the wrong picture without a warning. Could break: a workflow that relies on --dry to reset durations to estimates (none documented).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a dry run never replaces a measured clip length
Before: walked: a beat with an mp3 on disk and a measured length gets the estimate after --dry (narrate.mjs:371-386)
After: not built
Method: simulation - the round's narrate experiment (temp-copy tree, --dry) can take the figure if it first plants an mp3 and a measured entry; not run this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: the round's probe-narrate.mjs on a temp-copy tree: plant B.mp3 and a measured durations entry, run --dry, assert the entry is unchanged

title: shutdown removes the scratch database 500 ms after taskkill with no retry
body:
## Summary
On Windows, shutdown deletes the run's scratch directory half a second after taskkill and without retries, so a SQLite file the dying next dev still holds can make rmSync throw from afterAll.

## Description
examples/journey/src/boot.ts:168 waits a fixed 500 ms after `taskkill /T /F` (which returns before the tree's handles close) and :172 calls rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true }); force ignores ENOENT only, so EBUSY/EPERM on data/<app>.sqlite throws out of shutdown, out of the spec's afterAll, and the remaining apps in the loop are never shut down (tests/journey.spec.ts:132 awaits each in turn). Node's rmSync takes maxRetries/retryDelay for exactly this. Fixed: rmSync with maxRetries and retryDelay, and shutdown of one app never stopping the next (try/finally in the loop or per-app catch that logs).

## Flow
- afterAll -> shutdown(ledgerbox) -> taskkill -> 500 ms -> rmSync scratch
- next dev's sqlite handle not yet released -> EBUSY
- throw: hirelane, tidycrm and the outside server are never killed; ports 3002/3004/3005 stay held
- the next run refuses: 'something is already listening on 3002'

## Expected impact
A Windows operator re-running the journey finds orphaned dev servers holding the ports. Could break: nothing in the happy path; retries only delay a failing delete.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one app's teardown failure never leaves the others running
Before: not measured; the race needs the real next dev tree on Windows
After: not built
Method: simulation - three walked cases (fast release: fine; slow release: EBUSY throws; throw mid-loop: later apps orphaned); the instrument is the journey run, which this round may not start
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: the journey run on Windows by the operator (JOURNEY_PORT_OFFSET clear of the held 3001), repeated 5x, counting EBUSY from shutdown and ports left held after the run

title: an in-band tool failure is ledgered as outcome ok
body:
## Summary
When a page tool's handler throws or aborts, the kit door answers the text {"ok":false,"error":...} and the bridge reports ok:true, so Surface.run writes an `ok` row for a failed call.

## Description
examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/door.ts:75 toolError returns the failure as the tool's output string; packages/athena-bridge/inject.js:133 wraps any output in { ok: true, output }; examples/journey/src/surface.ts:227 then records outcome "ok". The act 4 record and the take's record page therefore count a handler fault as a success (invariant 6 asks for failures with a reason). The product path does the same (src/athena/contracts/registry.py builds ToolResult ok from the bridge's flag), so fixing only the journey would make the journey's record disagree with the daemon's on the same call; the registry map already records a sibling deviation for ledgerbox (mcp-tools, BooksTools.tsx:217). Deciding it needs the contract call: does the bridge or the registry read the in-band flag, and what reason does it map to.

## Flow
- a page tool handler throws -> door: '{"ok":false,"error":"tool failed: ..."}'
- inject.js: { ok: true, output: that text }
- Surface.run: ledger row outcome ok, reason null
- act 4 / record page: the failure counts as one of the calls that worked

## Expected impact
The record a person reads after a run understates failures. Could break: any consumer that treats the output text as data when ok is true.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failed tool call is recorded as refused with a reason, on every surface
Before: walked: a throwing handler yields an ok row (door.ts:123 -> inject.js:133 -> surface.ts:227)
After: not built - contract decision
Method: simulation - the chain is read end to end; a probe on the journey alone would only move the disagreement
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
